candidates.explanation: The exclusion filter is `id: Not(Number(conditions.userId))`. It compares the session id against the user id, when it should compare it against the id of the session to keep (`excludeId`). The soft-delete therefore removes every session of the user, including the current one. It spares only a session whose numeric id happens to equal the user id, and that is an unrelated session. This matches the report: the refresh call from the current device gets 401, and an unrelated older session sometimes survives.

The snippet is truncated, so I could not see the filter. The Mongo variant has to use `_id: { $not: { $eq: excludeId } }`. If it uses the user id or the wrong field here, the current session would be deleted in the same way.

The snippet is truncated, so I could not see the `deleteByUserIdWithExclude` call after the password change. If it passes `excludeId` as the user id instead of `userJwtPayload.sessionId`, the current session is not excluded.

fix.description: Change the exclusion to the session id, not the user id. Use `user: { id: Number(conditions.userId) }, id: Not(Number(conditions.excludeId))`. Also check that AuthService.update passes `excludeId: userJwtPayload.sessionId`.
